# broadlink-remote

> Python CLI scripts to control air conditioners, TVs and other infrared devices through a BroadLink RM4 Mini, without the BroadLink app or a cloud account.
> 中文：BroadLink 博联 RM4 Mini 红外万能遥控脚本，免 App 配网，学习或计算红外码，命令行控制空调，支持 OpenWrt 路由器和 AI agent（OpenClaw）。

## Two ways to get IR codes
- Learn: point your remote at the RM4 and run `ac_control.py learn <name>`. Try this first; works for most remotes.
- Calculate: when learning fails (signal too long or complex), build the code from the AC protocol bytes (see IRremoteESP8266) with `encode_broadlink()` in `tcl_send.py`.

## Two senders
- `scripts/ac_control.py`: discover, learn and send; needs `pip install broadlink` (PC / Raspberry Pi).
- `scripts/bl_send.py`: send only; needs just python3 and the `openssl` CLI, so it can run on OpenWrt routers. Accepts hex or base64 codes.

## Scripts
- `scripts/wifi_setup.py`: set up the device's WiFi without the official app
- `scripts/discover.py`: find the device on the LAN and save its info
- `scripts/ac_control.py`: learn and send IR codes, AC shortcuts (on/off/temp/mode)
- `scripts/bl_send.py`: zero-dependency sender
- `scripts/ac.sh`: call the router-side sender over SSH
- `scripts/tcl_send.py`: TCL AC code candidates generated from protocol bytes
- `scripts/tcl_ir_analysis.py`: TCL112AC protocol analysis

## Requirements
- Python 3; `requirements.txt` pins the broadlink library range (not needed by `bl_send.py`)
- Everything runs over the local network; no internet or cloud needed

## Limitations
- Only a TCL protocol example is included; other brands need their own protocol bytes
- Only used with an RM4 Mini by the author
- Command-line only
